title: Precision Apiary Console (simulated bee yard, one season)

tools.name: get_hives
tools.description: List the hives in the yard with their current placement and last-recorded state (population, brood, stores).

tools.name: inspect_hive
tools.description: Open one hive and return a detailed inspection: brood pattern, population trend, and any field-visible health signs. More revealing than the summary in get_hives.

tools.name: pest_pressure
tools.description: Return measured pest indicators (e.g. varroa mite count per 100 bees) for a hive. Requires a scheduled inspection to have a sample; otherwise returns the last lab reading or 'no sample'.

tools.name: forage_map
tools.description: Return the forage sources currently blooming this season, each with location, nectar quality, and bloom status. This is the LIVE map for this year.

tools.name: weather_season
tools.description: Return the season weather outlook by week (temperature, rain) — context for bloom timing and inspection planning.

tools.name: harvest_forecast
tools.description: Return the projected honey-flow curve by week (relative nectar income), so you can judge when stores will peak. Does not name a date — you read the curve.

tools.name: schedule_inspection
tools.description: Schedule an inspection of a hive in a given week. This is what produces a fresh pest sample for pest_pressure.

tools.name: treat
tools.description: Apply a mite/disease treatment to a hive in a given week. Treating costs effort and stresses a healthy colony — only treat what needs it, and in time.

tools.name: place_hive
tools.description: Move/place a hive at a forage location for the season. Good placement is near a source that is actually blooming this year.

tools.name: harvest
tools.description: Pull honey supers from a hive in a given week. Harvesting too early or too late costs yield and can leave the colony short on winter stores.

tools.name: close_season
tools.description: End the season and submit your apiary for grading. Returns the graded outcome (colony survival + harvest yield).
